import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import colorsys

img = np.array(Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')).astype(float)
h, w, _ = img.shape
# Columns of the barcode = stripes
cols = img[::4, :, :]  # sample rows
avg = cols.mean(axis=0)  # (w,3)

# Per-column stats
r,g,b = avg[:,0], avg[:,1], avg[:,2]
mx = avg.max(axis=1); mn = avg.min(axis=1)
val = mx/255.0
sat = np.where(mx>0, (mx-mn)/np.maximum(mx,1), 0)

print("Overall mean RGB:", avg.mean(axis=0).round(1))
print("Mean brightness (val):", val.mean().round(3))
print("Mean saturation:", sat.mean().round(3))
print("Max per-column saturation:", sat.max().round(3))
print("Fraction of columns with sat>0.3:", (sat>0.3).mean().round(3))
print("Fraction of columns with sat>0.4:", (sat>0.4).mean().round(3))
print("Fraction of columns with val<0.25:", (val<0.25).mean().round(3))
print("Fraction of columns with val>0.7:", (val>0.7).mean().round(3))

# Hue distribution for saturated columns
hues = []
for i in range(w):
    if sat[i] > 0.25:
        hh, ss, vv = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(r[i]/255, g[i]/255, b[i]/255)
        hues.append(hh*360)
hues = np.array(hues)
if len(hues):
    hist, edges = np.histogram(hues, bins=12, range=(0,360))
    for i in range(12):
        print(f" hue {edges[i]:.0f}-{edges[i+1]:.0f}: {hist[i]}")

# Print stripe sequence: group consecutive columns with similar color
def cval(i): return tuple(avg[i].astype(int))
groups=[]
cur=[0,cval(0)]
for i in range(1,w):
    c=cval(i)
    if max(abs(c[k]-cur[1][k]) for k in range(3))<=8:
        cur[1]=c
    else:
        groups.append((cur[0], i-1, cur[1]))
        cur=[i,c]
groups.append((cur[0], w-1, cur[1]))
print("\nNumber of distinct color runs:", len(groups))
print("First 30 runs (start,end,RGB):")
for gstart, gend, c in groups[:30]:
    print(f"  {gstart:4d}-{gend:4d} len{gend-gstart+1:4d}  RGB{c}")
EOF
